false_positives.candidate:
Already-committed migration changed to force: true

An existing migration was edited to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. Editing a migration that may already have been applied in deployments has no effect there, while `force: true` silently drops any pre-existing `top_topics` table (and its data) on environments where the migration runs after the table exists. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table. Prefer a new migration or drop the `force` flag.

Kernel#open on remote URL relies on open-uri being loaded and follows redirects to arbitrary hosts

`import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri` (only `poll_feed.rb` does). If the RetrieveTopic job runs in a process where open-uri hasn't been loaded by something else, `open` is `Kernel#open` on a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for `http://...`. Additionally, even with open-uri, redirects from the (host-validated) embeddable host are followed to any destination, so a redirect to an internal address lets an anonymous user make the server fetch internal resources and publish the readability-extracted content as a topic. Use an explicit HTTP client with redirect control and require it explicitly.

Test description says 404 but missing embed_url yields 400 and test only asserts non-success

`params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, which is rendered as 400, not 404 as the spec title claims. The assertion `response.should_not be_success` would also pass if the action raised any unrelated error (e.g. the referer check failing first), so it does not verify the intended behavior. absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

`href.start_with?('/')` is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. When the refreshed response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers then copy this into the stored credential: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` (line 120 of zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts) and Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over `o365AuthCredentials` (line 264 of office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, where `refresh_token` is `.optional()`). true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]"; all non-access_token fields are stripped

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are JavaScript computed property keys; calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object yields the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. Both keys collide (the second wins), so the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when credential sync is enabled every expiry/scope/instance_url field is dropped from the parsed result and no numeric expiry is ever validated. Downstream, Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN, Office365 never gets an updated `expires_in`, and Salesforce loses `instance_url`/`id`/`signature` from the stored key. Use `.passthrough()` / `z.record` or an explicit refinement instead of computed keys.

Several of the defects above (computed-key schema, SafeParse wrapper being persisted, Response vs. object shape mismatches, missing prisma import) would be caught by even minimal unit tests of the helpers with sync enabled/disabled and a type-check run.

Outbound request to the credential sync endpoint carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret/header. The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so a self-hoster following this contract must expose an unauthenticated token oracle (or invent out-of-band auth). The inbound webhook uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; the outbound call should send the same shared secret so the self-hoster can verify requests.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`

The shared secret header is compared using plain string inequality, which is susceptible to timing side channels. Also, if the configured header appears multiple times `req.headers[...]` is a `string[]` and the comparison always fails. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and normalize the header to a single string.

`prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
